title: Politics, not law, is the way to defeat the illiberals
gist: DAT Green argues that constitutional reform and legal prosecution are not the way to defeat illiberal politicians; only political organisation and mobilisation can. He cites recent defeats or setbacks for illiberals in Serbia, Brazil and Israel across different constitutional forms, and expects Democratic gains in the US midterms while noting the US separation of powers failed when it mattered.

insights.claim: DAT Green argues it does not matter what form a constitution takes if those with power act unconstitutionally; the US constitution already allows Trump to be checked at every step but those with checks have chosen not to use them.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Institutional safeguards cannot be relied upon to constrain policy risk; political dynamics dominate.
insights.quote: For it does not matter whatsoever what form a constitution takes if those with power act unconstitutionally.

insights.claim: Russia and Weimar Germany both had codified constitutions with liberal-looking provisions that counted for nothing in practice.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Formal legal protections are weak indicators of actual governance risk.
insights.locator: Codified constitutions are not a universal

insights.claim: Green says the famed US separation of powers failed when it mattered over the last two years, a revelation that cannot be unlearned, and the federal judiciary and Supreme Court are tame in the face of Trump's abuses.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Lasting erosion of perceived US institutional reliability is a structural factor for US risk premia.
insights.quote: We now all know that the famed separation of powers in the US constitution failed when it mattered.

insights.claim: In recent elections, Serbia's Student List won a parliamentary majority defeating the incumbent rightist government, Lula da Silva held off Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil, and Netanyahu's coalition lost a significant number of seats in Israel.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Political change in Serbia, Brazil and Israel may shift policy direction and country risk.

insights.claim: These outcomes occurred under different constitutional forms, with Serbia and Brazil codified and Israel uncodified, showing constitutional form is not decisive; as Orbán found in Hungary, fairly free elections can cost illiberals power.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Electoral competitiveness, not legal form, is the key indicator for assessing illiberal regime durability.

insights.claim: Green expects Trump's attempts to rig the US midterms not to succeed and anticipates his supporters will switch to delegitimising the results.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Post-election contestation could add US political volatility.

insights.claim: Democrats are expected to make significant gains in the US midterms, possibly winning both houses of Congress, which could resume some checks and balances.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Divided government would constrain executive policy and shift US fiscal and regulatory outlook.

insights.claim: Green lists a Spanish general election soon after the US midterms and the French presidential election next year as further tests of an apparent liberal turn.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: European election calendar is a source of political risk to monitor.

insights.claim: Brazil prosecuted and convicted Jair Bolsonaro for plotting a coup, yet the recent presidential election was still close-run, showing legal accountability alone does not solve political problems.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Legal outcomes against populist leaders don't eliminate their political base or associated policy risk.

insights.claim: Marine Le Pen's National Rally has a strong chance of success in next year's French presidential election despite her conviction for misusing EU funds, which has made no real political difference.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Elevated probability of a National Rally win is a key 2027 French and EU political risk.

insights.claim: Green concludes that illiberal electoral blocs are political problems requiring political solutions, especially organising and mobilising opposition, which is far harder than amending a constitution.
insights.speaker: DAT Green
insights.so_what: Assess populist risk by tracking opposition strength rather than legal constraints.
